hints: Look closely at the structure and spot the two different carbonyl groups present in this small molecule.
Notice the left side is a $\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}$ methyl carbonyl unit, while the right side is a $\text{-CHO}$ aldehyde unit.
Check each test in turn: iodoform needs a methyl carbonyl, 2,4-DNPH needs any aldehyde or ketone, and Fehling's needs an aldehyde.
walkthrough:
**Identify the functional groups**

Great start, let's read the structure. The compound is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCHO}$, called methylglyoxal.

It has two carbonyls in one molecule: a ketone on the left and an aldehyde on the right.

**Test 1 - alkaline aqueous iodine**

This is the iodoform test for the $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ group or $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)-}$ group.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CO- + I}_2 + \text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{CHI}_3 \text{ (yellow ppt)}$$ 
Since we have $\text{CH}_3\text{-C=O-}$, test 1 is positive.

**Test 2 - 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine**

This is Brady's reagent. It gives an orange precipitate with any aldehyde or ketone.

$$\text{C=O + H}_2\text{NNHC}_6\text{H}_3(\text{NO}_2)_2 \rightarrow \text{hydrazone (orange ppt) + H}_2\text{O}$$
Our molecule has both, so test 2 is definitely positive.

**Test 3 - Fehling's solution**

Fehling's solution is a mild oxidising agent that is reduced by aliphatic aldehydes to brick-red $\text{Cu}_2\text{O}$.

$$\text{RCHO + 2Cu}^{2+} + 5\text{OH}^- \rightarrow \text{RCOO}^- + \text{Cu}_2\text{O + 3H}_2\text{O}$$
Because we have a $\text{-CHO}$ group, test 3 is also positive. All three are correct.

options.A: Correct. All of 1, 2 and 3 are positive. The $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ part gives the iodoform reaction, the carbonyl groups give the 2,4-DNPH reaction, and the $\text{-CHO}$ part gives the Fehling's reaction.
options.B: Incorrect. This combination includes only 1 and 2. It wrongly leaves out Fehling's solution. Students choose this if they focus only on the ketone on the left and forget the aldehyde on the right is easily oxidised.
options.C: Incorrect. This combination includes only 2 and 3. It wrongly leaves out alkaline aqueous iodine. Students choose this if they remember the aldehyde tests but forget that $\text{CH}_3\text{CO-}$ is the classic positive group for the iodoform test.
options.D: Incorrect. This is 1 only. It wrongly leaves out the two most obvious carbonyl tests. Students choose this if they think only one functional group can react, missing that this molecule is both an aldehyde and a methyl ketone.
